clue.text: Pay attention to appropriate review

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it for yourself
a review of a play or book is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to heed a fitting critique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective describing the review, but it is the verb, seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to observe it closely, an everyday idiom for paying attention.

clue.text: Quarrel, though fair-spoken in French

definitions.meaning: the French 'tout doux', meaning very gently or softly, is pronounced the same way as the answer

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: a row is anything but gentle, though the French phrase for 'very gently' (tout doux) sounds identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or commotion, as in 'what a to-do', is a squabble; and the French phrase 'tout doux', said aloud, matches it.

clue.text: Recoil from excitement

definitions.meaning: a gun's ... is its backward jolt when fired
a ... is a thrill, as in doing something for ...

explanation.definitionFit: A rifle's backward jerk and a thrill share one word, as in 'get a kick out of it'.

clue.text: Heath, following morning, supports PM in this part of the world

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece supports the upper, so the prime minister's name sits on top

parts.note: Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence

indicators.note: following places the word for heath after the one for morning

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning
erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: Edward Heath, after a morning, propping up a prime minister somewhere in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' and 'PM' together suggest Edward Heath, the 1970s British Prime Minister; here Heath is the plant and the PM is Lord North. 'following' and 'supports' put the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent containing Canada, the USA and Mexico is a region of the globe.

clue.text: Art patron and monarch — King Edward, perhaps

parts.note: Sir Henry Tate, sugar magnate, founded the Tate Gallery in London
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts and a king, perhaps a royal Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British variety of potato, and a tater is slang for a potato, so the royal-sounding definition is a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a British potato variety, and a spud is colloquially called a tater.

clue.text: On dropping off diamond, relative gets another gem

indicators.note: dropping off signals that the word on is removed from the synonym for diamond

parts.note: diamond is a crystalline form of carbon
the word on, taken as written
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A diamond falls off, and a relative receives a different jewel instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' takes ON from CARBON, leaving CARB.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, typically a garnet cut with a rounded top.

clue.text: One's perplexed at a defeat like this

definitions.meaning: someone puzzled is said to be 'at a ...', so the missing word completes the idiom

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is one phrase with a gap: the perplexed person is 'at a' something, and that something is also a defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'at a loss' is the idiom for puzzlement, and a beaten team suffers a reverse in a game.

clue.text: Works to conceal evening wear

parts.note: opera is the plural of opus, a work
to cloak something is to hide it

explanation.walkthrough: OPERA is the plural of the Latin opus, a convention setters use for 'works'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long cape worn over formal dress for a night at the theatre is classic formal attire.

clue.text: Cut of meat sea-cook left, perhaps

parts.note: Long John Silver is the ship's cook in Treasure Island
left is one side, right being the other

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut, maybe left by a ship's cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks left as one example of a side. Silverside is a British joint of beef from the outer thigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a British beef joint from the hindquarter, usually salted or roasted.

clue.text: They adorn the house, as speakers, after a month

indicators.note: after places the speakers behind the month in the answer

parts.note: DEC is short for December
orators are public speakers

explanation.surface: Orators arriving a month later to brighten up a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They adorn the house' suggests ornaments or flowers, but it means people who paint and paper homes; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters and paperhangers make a home look attractive, so they are its embellishers.

clue.text: Rock and roll music

definitions.meaning: to sway or stagger, rocking and rolling on your feet
a lively Scottish or Irish dance tune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' looks like the music genre, but it is the verb, to lurch about; the answer is also a folk dance tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger dizzily is to lurch from side to side, and a Scottish dance tune shares the name.

clue.text: Excessively prettified brown tree

parts.note: chocolate is a shade of brown
box is a small evergreen tree used for hedging

explanation.walkthrough: Old sweet boxes bore sentimental pictures of thatched cottages and kittens, hence the adjective for sugary prettiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet tins once carried twee rural scenes, so the phrase now means sentimentally pretty, like a picture postcard.

clue.text: Poetic though raw food, in a way

parts.note: tho' is the clipped form of though used in verse
rough means crude, unrefined
fare is food, as on a menu

explanation.surface: Somewhat verse-like, though uncooked food is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or street through a town is a route, a public way.

clue.text: Indirect, as some judges are?

definitions.meaning: circuit judges travel from court to court around a region, and the question mark admits the pun

explanation.walkthrough: In England, circuit judges hear cases at a circuit of courts around a region, so the second reading is a pun on 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout route avoids the direct line; circuit judges tour a circuit of courts.

clue.text: A part in play cut? Steps showing powerful influence

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the scene loses its last letter

parts.note: a scene is a division of a play
a dance is a series of steps

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a role in a play was trimmed, then shows impressive footwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final E of SCENE, leaving SCEN; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance or sway over others is supremacy, a controlling power.

clue.text: Changing main coins, unable to get rest

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of main coins are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone up all night exchanging the main currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges MAIN COINS. The definition, unable to rest, works as a description of a sleepless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually cannot sleep is a chronic sufferer of sleeplessness.

clue.text: One sort — nine or ten iron — is involved, in addition

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Golf talk: picking a club, say nine iron or ten iron, while adding something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or ten iron' is surface padding; 'is involved' rearranges I, SORT and NINE. 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put into a text is an addition, like an inserted paragraph.

clue.text: Gunman's young team

definitions.meaning: Samuel Colt, inventor of the revolver, the possessive giving the s
a ... side is a junior team of young players

explanation.walkthrough: Colts is the British term for youth teams in sport, from young horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Colt made the famous revolver, and junior sports sides are called colts after young horses.

clue.text: Jump over net

definitions.meaning: to ... a fence is to leap it
to make it as profit after costs

explanation.walkthrough: 'net' looks like a noun for a mesh, but it is the verb meaning to earn after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler gets over an obstacle; net profit is what you make after expenses.

clue.text: West Indian players harden resolve of all-rounder

parts.note: to steel yourself is to harden your resolve
a band goes all the way round something, like a ring

explanation.surface: Caribbean cricketers firming up the determination of their versatile player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-rounder' looks like a cricketer who bats and bowls, but it means a ring encircling something. Steel bands, playing oil-drum pans, come from Trinidad.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinidad's pan orchestras of tuned oil drums are Caribbean musicians.

clue.text: To mould opinion in party, interact oddly

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Political advice: at a party gathering, mingle in odd ways to shape views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' tells you to rearrange INTERACT, which gives CTRINATE. 'party' is the crossword staple for DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil beliefs systematically shapes what people think, a propaganda sense.

clue.text: European inventor inferior to. American one, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: someone no match for the American inventor Alexander Graham Bell is no Bell

explanation.surface: A European inventor reckoned lesser than an American counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish inventor of dynamite, sounds like 'no Bell', i.e. not up to Bell, inventor of the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, a Swede, invented dynamite and endowed the prizes.

clue.text: Part of speech delivered, for example

definitions.meaning: the word delivered is a doing word, an example of the class

explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' tempts as a link meaning spoken; it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doing word is a grammatical class, and 'delivered' is one such action word.

clue.text: Sin that's representative, nonetheless

indicators.note: read as none the less: nothing, the letter O, is taken away

parts.note: an envoy represents a government abroad

explanation.surface: A diplomat committing a deadly sin anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' splits as 'none the less': O (nothing) removed from ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetousness is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Is responsible for private school's head

parts.note: your own things are private to you

indicators.note: head means the first letter of school

explanation.surface: Who is in charge of a private school's headteacher?
explanation.walkthrough: 'private school' reads as one phrase, but 'private' gives OWN and 'school's head' the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing something makes you answerable for it, as an owner holds title.

clue.text: African bishop we installed in Zambian parts

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside, so these letters go into the other group
parts as a verb means separates, so the letters of Zambian are broken up and reordered

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop and his flock established in regions of Zambia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' is the anagram signal and 'installed in' the container signal; the surface reads it as regions of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Zimbabwe is a southern African.

clue.text: Dispatched in turn

definitions.meaning: to swing round, as a ship or vehicle ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatched' looks like sent off, but it is the euphemism for killed; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaying is killing, so a dispatched foe was killed; a skidding car swings round sideways.

clue.text: Fix line by changing about fifty in rigid fashion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the extra letter
changing tells us the letters of fix line by are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A repair instruction: fix the line by altering roughly fifty, rigidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about fifty' reads as 'roughly fifty', but 'about' says the rearranged letters go round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffly and unbendingly means without any give, so rigidly.
